meaning: Light – the gematria value of the Hebrew word "אור" (or, 'light')
description: The number 207 appears in the Bible as the number of years Reu lived after he had his son Serug (Gen 11:21), as part of the lineage from Shem to Abraham. Although the number is not directly assigned symbolic meaning in the biblical text, it has held an important place in Jewish tradition through gematria: 207 is the numerical value of the Hebrew word "אור" (or), which means "light." Light is one of the most fundamental concepts in Scripture – the first thing God created when he spoke the words "Let there be light!" (Gen 1:3). This connection has made 207 a number with deep resonance in kabbalistic thought, where light represents divine revelation, wisdom, and God's presence.

versions.meaning: The number 207 has no well-established symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition.
versions.description: 207 is not a number highlighted specifically in the Bible or in traditional Jewish numerology (gematria) with any widely recognized symbolic meaning. In Hebrew gematria, 207 corresponds to the numerical value of the word "אור" (or), which means 'light', giving the number a certain mystical association in Kabbalistic circles. Nevertheless, this is an derived interpretation and not a direct biblical symbolism tied to the number 207 itself.

footnotes.text: The gematria value of "אור" is calculated as follows: alef (א) = 1, vav (ו) = 6, resh (ר) = 200, which together give 207.

In Kabbalistic literature, especially in the Zohar, 'or' (light) is a central concept denoting the divine light that flows through the sefirot system. The fact that this word's numerical value is 207 gives the number a special mystical significance in meditative and contemplative Jewish practice.

Reu (רְעוּ) was the father of Serug and the great-grandfather of Terah, Abraham's father. His lifespan of 207 years after Serug's birth is part of the systematic decline in longevity described in the genealogy in Genesis 11.
